## Lab 6 Specifications

Lab 6 asks you to build a complete IoT device on top of a driver you write yourself against the DS1722 register map. The main focus of your driver implementation is enabling SPI communication, and understanding of serial communication is a major learning goal for the lab.

### Hardware Specifications

#### Proficiency

- [ ] DS1722 temperature sensor is correctly wired per its datasheet pinout and is powered by 3.3V.
- [ ] System correctly reads the current temperature from the DS1722 sensor and displays it on a webpage that updates the temperature when refreshed.
- [ ] Webpage displays the current LED state and can toggle it.

#### Excellence

- [ ] User can select the DS1722's resolution (e.g., 8/9/10/11/12-bit) from the webpage, and the driver correctly reconfigures the sensor in response.

### Software and Microcontroller Design Specifications

#### Proficiency

- [ ] SPI device driver is written using the CMSIS device templates (register structs and base addresses from `stm32l432xx.h`), not a third-party, copied driver or home-grown driver.

#### Excellence

- [ ] Test exists that the system can support the -10&deg;C to 30&deg;C range.

### Other Documentation

#### Proficiency

- [ ] Report includes a logic analyzer capture of a full SPI read transaction (CE, SCK, SDO and SDI), labeled with bit values and bit period, showing that the frequency is less than 5 Hz.

#### Excellence

- [ ] Logic analyzer capture is annotated to show how the observed timing matches the datasheet's specified SPI timing.
